hints: Comparing every pair works, but it's O(n²). What would let you check a value against *everything before it* at once?
Sorting puts equal values side by side - then you only compare neighbours.
A hash set answers "have I seen this?" in O(1). One pass is enough.

insight.oneLiner: Remember everything you've passed in a hash set; a duplicate is any value that's already there.

recall.a: Pairs O(n²)/O(1); sort O(n log n)/O(1)-ish; hash set O(n)/O(n).
recall.q: What are the three approaches and their costs?

recall.a: The first repeat proves the answer is true - no need to look further.
recall.q: Why can the hash-set loop return early?

insight.why: Each membership check is O(1) on average, so the whole scan is O(n) - at the price of O(n) extra memory.

oneLiner: Remember everything you've passed in a hash set; a duplicate is any value that's already there.

pitfalls.explain: If the inner loop starts at i instead of i + 1, every element 'matches' itself.
pitfalls.title: Compared an element with itself

pitfalls.explain: A `return False` inside the loop gives up after the first comparison. You can only conclude 'no duplicates' after the loop finishes.
pitfalls.title: Returned False before checking everything

solutions.idea: For each element, scan everything after it for an equal value.
solutions.name: Compare every pair

solutions.idea: After sorting, any duplicates are adjacent, so a single neighbour comparison pass finds them.
solutions.name: Sort, then compare neighbours

solutions.idea: Walk the array once, keeping a set of values seen so far.
solutions.name: Hash set
